messages:
ara: Heads-up — automated access certification ran overnight. Summary: ~62 stale service accounts (no key rotation), 18 admin-role bindings >90d. Uploading CSV and proposing remediation flow.
infra-bot: certbot: Access certification completed. Report: https://internal.redwood/reports/access-cert/2026-03-19 (csv attached)
sam: Thanks. Can we get a CSV export with these columns: owner, last_used, linked_kms_key, role_bindings, suggested_action?
ara: Yes — CSV will include those columns plus a severity flag. Quick remediation playbook idea: 1) notify owners via PR, 2) auto-tag orphan accounts and schedule 30-day expiry, 3) rotate keys and attach CMK where applicable. Thoughts?
dina: 30-day expiry is aggressive for some infra svcaccts used by legacy CI. Can we allow a 90d window for infra-sre-reviewed infra?
jess: Agreed — also recommend forcing CMK attachment and ensuring CloudAudit logs are enabled for decrypt operations. Audit logs should ship to central bucket.
mike: For automation, add a precondition in CI (prow) to reject jobs if they use unrotated keys or orphan svcaccts. That will reduce surprise breakages.
ara: Good. Proposed two-track flow: automated revocation for true-orphans (no owner + no usage) and a manual review queue for flagged infra. We'll do a canary rollout to avoid large outages.
sam: How does certbot decide "no owner" today? Labels are optional in some projects. Can it cross-check GitHub CODEOWNERS or oncall roster?
ara: certbot owner detection order: service-account label -> GitHub CODEOWNERS -> last-modifier in infra repo. If none found, marks "orphan". We can extend heuristics.
dina: Also need detection of what KMS key is used. Lots of svcaccts still use project-level keys instead of CMKs. Would like a migration recommendation column.
ara: I'll add KMS-key detection and a recommended migration step. Example detection query I used in the audit: ```gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=svc-foo@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format='json(name,validAfterTime,validBeforeTime)'```
jess: For rotation, are we auto-rotating keys or just creating tickets? We need a zero-downtime rotation pattern documented.
ara: Plan: auto-rotate keys for "managed" svcaccts via k8s-secrets-sync job (update secret -> rotate -> switch), and for sensitive/legacy ones create a ticket with step-by-step rotation + rollback doc.
mike: Can we run a dry-run revoke in staging against ~50 accounts and surface failing jobs so owners can fix? I can own that run.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: staging job queued: certbot-remediation-dryrun-2026-03-20 (job id: cb-dryrun-342)
jess: :thumbsup: please include log retention for the dry-run so we can debug failures.
sam: Timeline?
ara: Draft remediation PR by EOD Thursday, canary dry-run Friday, targeted owner notices Monday, org-wide enforcement after 2-week notice.
dina: Add an "exempted" tag for long-lived infra accounts with a justification doc and infra-sre sign-off. We'll keep a short-lived exemption TTL (max 180d) and require re-approval.
mike: I'll volunteer to run the canary and monitor logs. Will also coordinate with oncall if we see job failures.
ara: Thanks — assigning owners: @mike = canary owner, @dina = exemption triage, @sam = CSV schema review. I'll open the PR and ping teams. Please react on the PR if you approve. :white_check_mark:
ara: One quick note: we should also tie entitlement cleanup into quarterly RBAC reviews so this doesn't pile up. I'll add a follow-up ticket to eng-sre backlog.
